headline: Japan's visitor arrivals fell 5% in September to 3.10 million, but tourist spending rose.
body: Arrivals from China fell 44.5% to 430,800, while spending by visitors in July to September was an estimated ¥2.21 trillion, up 3.2%. January to September arrivals were 30.73 million, down 2.9%; the UK row of the September release was not in the coverage found.
why: With Chinese demand collapsing, Japan's tourism bodies lean harder on long-haul markets such as the UK, whose own growth slowed to 5.8% for January to August.
